Ambrose Bierce-Hare and Tortoise
A Hare having ridiculed the slow movements of a Tortoise, was challenged by the latter to run a race, a Fox to go to the goal and be the judge. They got off well together, the hare at the top of her speed, the Tortoise, who had no other intention than making his antagonist exert herself, going very leisurely. After sauntering along for some time he discovered the Hare by the wayside, apparently asleep, and seeing a chance to win pushed on as fast as he could, arriving at the goal hours afterward, suffering from extreme fatigue and claiming the victory.
"Not so," said the Fox; "the Hare was here long ago, and went back to cheer you on your way."

texts.text:
A Hare having ridiculed the slow movements of a Tortoise, 
was challenged by the latter to run a race, a Fox to go to the 
goal and be the judge. They got off well together, the hare at 
the top of her speed, the Tortoise, who had no other intention 
than making his antagonist exert herself, going very leisurely. 
After sauntering along for some time he discovered the Hare 
by the wayside, apparently asleep, and seeing a chance to win 
pushed on as fast as he could, arriving at the goal hours 
afterward, suffering from extreme fatigue and claiming the 
victory.

"Not so," said the Fox; "the Hare was here long 
ago, and went back to cheer you on your way."

pages.html:
Ambrose Bierce-Hare and Tortoise Unlike the traditional tale where the hare's arrogance and overconfidence lead to his defeat, this version highlights the hare's awareness and sportsmanship. The hare not only wins the race but also shows humility by returning to cheer on the tortoise.
Meanwhile, the tortoise's slow pace and eventual fatigue emphasize the limits of perseverance when it is not matched with a realistic understanding of the situation.
1. True success is not just about winning but about showing kindness and humility, uplifting others even in moments of triumph
2. Perseverance alone is not enough; it must be paired with a realistic understanding of one's limitations and the situation to achieve true success.

What is THEME?
DEFINITIOON
It is the underlying meaning of a story and embodies general truths about society or human nature. (p.7)
The theme is the central meaning of the narrative. It has been called the worldview, philosophy, message, or moral lesson within a story. (p.109)
A theme connects a profound idea about our world to the events within a text. It reflects the central concept you wish to share with your readers, one that has the potential to inspire, provoke thought, and transform perspectives.

Figurative Language: Understatement
Definition:
Understatement is a figure of speech in which something is expressed less strongly than would be expected, or in which something is presented as being smaller, worse, or lesser than it really is. Typically, understatement is used to call attention to the very quality it pretends to downplay.

Figurative Language: Understatement
Definition:
1) Understatement is a figure of speech. Understatement deliberately makes a situation less important or serious than it is (p.131).
2) It deliberately represents something as very much less in magnitude or importance than it really is, or is ordinarily considered to be. The effect is usually ironic (2014:167).

Figurative Language: OnomatopoeiaDefinition:
Onomatopoeia is a figure of speech in which words evoke the actual sound of the thing they refer to or describe. The “boom” of a firework exploding, the “tick tock” of a clock, and the “ding dong” of a doorbell are all examples of onomatopoeia.

Activity 10: Using Figurative Devices
Tanysha sat up late in her bedroom silently and studiously trying to study.
She was such a great student that anything less than a 100++ would send her sobbing from the room.
Tomorrow’s math test was as important to Tanysha as a candidate’s final election speech is in the presidential election.
With a squeak of bedsprings and the crunch of crumpled paper, Tanysha lay back on her bed for a minute.
She started daydreaming about going to the ivory tower learning to become a disease fighter one day.
1) Using Alliteration: Tanysha sat up late in her bedroom trying to study.
2) Using Hyperbole: She was an all-A student...
3) Using Simile: ... and tomorrow's math test was an important one.
4) Using Onomatopoeia: Lying back on her bed for a minute.
5) Using Metaphor: ... Tanysha started daydreaming about going to college and
becoming a doctor one day.
